Q: How to Insert datas from a dataframe into a database? A:

Update your load_weather_data function to correct the to_sql arguments and re-raise the exception at the end of the except block so Airflow can track failures properly.

import os 
import pandas as pd 
from dotenv import load_dotenv 
from config.database import engine 

load_dotenv() 

def load_weather_data(data): 
    try: 
        print(f"\n=== DÉBOGAGE ===") 
        print(f"hourly_df - shape: {data['hourly_df'].shape}, vide: {data['hourly_df'].empty}") 
        print(f"daily_df - shape: {data['daily_df'].shape}, vide: {data['daily_df'].empty}") 
        
        # --- FIXED HOURLY LOAD ---
        if not data['hourly_df'].empty: 
            print(f"hourly_df colonnes: {list(data['hourly_df'].columns)}") 
            print(f"hourly_df première ligne:\n{data['hourly_df'].head(1)}") 
            
            # Correct parameters: name first, then the engine connectable
            data["hourly_df"].to_sql(name="hourly_weather", con=engine, if_exists="append", index=False) 
            print("✓ hourly_weather chargé avec succès") 
        else:
            print("⚠️ hourly_df est vide, rien ne sera chargé") 

        # --- FIXED DAILY LOAD ---
        if not data['daily_df'].empty: 
            print(f"daily_df colonnes: {list(data['daily_df'].columns)}") 
            print(f"daily_df première ligne:\n{data['daily_df'].head(1)}") 
            
            data["daily_df"].to_sql(name="daily_weather", con=engine, if_exists="append", index=False) 
            print("✓ daily_weather chargé avec succès") 
        else: 
            print("⚠️ daily_df est vide, rien ne sera chargé") 
            
        print("Chargement terminé\n") 
        
    except Exception as e: 
        print(f"✗ Erreur lors du chargement: {e}") 
        raise e  # This allows Airflow to see the failure!

if __name__ == "__main__": 
    test_data = {"current_df": pd.DataFrame(), "hourly_df": pd.DataFrame(), "daily_df": pd.DataFrame()} 
    load_weather_data(test_data)

Q: Using VirtualEnv with multiple Python versions on Windows A:

Better is:

py -3.4 -m venv c:\path\to\wherever\you\want\it

If you don't have the py.exe launcher (but it should be installed), you can replace py -3.4 with c:\Python34\python.exe (assuming the default location).

This does require the selected Python runtime version to be installed on the machine. You can install any version via the Microsoft Store or by downloading its installer from the website.

This works because of the handy-dandy, Windows-versioningest, super nice runtime picker py.exe

By default, py.exe will be present on a Windows install (I think it comes with 2.7, I know it does with 3+). When you run py then it will search for some environment variables or you can override that with a specific version number (in your case -2.7or -3.4) You can leave off the .4 and it will choose the "biggest" minor version number.

You can also use it to run Python scripts. If you put a hash-bang line at the top of your script #!python3 and call it py myscript.py then it will pick the correct version of Python to start with, by searching the first line of the script and searching for a version number.

This is cool, because you can put something like #!/usr/bin/env python3.4 at the top of your script and run it on Windows with py, or on Linux by doing

chmod +x myscript.py
./myscript.py

It is pretty useful.

Q: How to replace zero values with NULL in Google BigQuery without syntax errors? A:

first your code contain a syntax error your code must look like this , Because ur code must contain the ELSE keyword

-- Source - https://stackoverflow.com/q/79974145
-- Posted by Spamr Spamr
-- Retrieved 2026-07-03, License - CC BY-SA 4.0

UPDATE `my_project.weather_data.tracks_2023`
SET 
  wind_speed = CASE WHEN wind_speed = 0 THEN ELSE wind_speed NULL END,
  visibility = CASE WHEN visibility = 0 THEN ELSE wind_speed NULL END
WHERE wind_speed = 0 OR visibility = 0;

and i recommend you to use the NULLIF() function who make your sql code much more readable

UPDATE `my_project.weather_data.tracks_2023`
SET
    wind_speed = NULLIF(wind_speed, 0),
    visibility = NULLIF(visibility, 0)
WHERE wind_speed = 0 OR visibility = 0;

Q: FlutterFlow Web App Shows Blank White Screen on First Load After Deployment A:

  1. When Bundle CanvasKit for Offline Use is enabled, the Flutter web engine automatically appends /chromium/

  2. yea. if you choose to host CanvasKit yourself (offline mode), you must upload the full unaltered canvaskit/ folder generated in Flutter's build/web directory.

  3. Yes, if you do not want to manage hosting the large WASM binary files manually, changing this string is the easiest fix.

In my opinion You should switch to Google's Global CDN

  1. Open your FlutterFlow Settings -> Web Delivery / CanvasKit settings.

  2. Keep CanvasKit Enabled: Yes.

  3. Set CanvasKit Base URL exactly to:
    https://www.gstatic.com/flutter-canvaskit/

  4. Change Bundle CanvasKit for Offline Use to: Disabled (Toggle off).

  5. Redeploy or rebuild your web app.

Q: How to read a group of a .zarr file using R? A:

With the file created by your python script I see, on Ubuntu and Windows, and with terra 1.9.34 (CRAN) and terra 1.9.38 (Dev):

library(terra)
#terra 1.9.38
rast("data.zarr", "vpd")
#class       : SpatRaster
#size        : 5, 8, 10  (nrow, ncol, nlyr)
#dimensions  : lon, lat, time (8, 5, 10}
#resolution  : 51.42857, 45  (x, y)
#extent      : -205.7143, 205.7143, -112.5, 112.5  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
#coord. ref. : 
#source      : data.zarr
#varname     : vpd/vpd
#names       : vpd_1, vpd_2, vpd_3, vpd_4, vpd_5, vpd_6, ...
#time (days) : 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-10 (10 steps)
#Warning message:
#shape missing or not an array (GDAL error 1)

(I think you can ignore the warning if you would even get it)

The reason that it does not work for you is clear from the warning you are getting

Decompressor blosc not handled (GDAL error 1)

This means that your GDAL was built without support for blosc compression. I assume you are on linux and may be able to fix your GDAL build. Otherwise the standard binary terra distributions should work (including r2u on Ubuntu)

I see:

gdalinfo --format Zarr
## skipping to the last line:
# BLOSC_COMPRESSORS=blosclz,lz4,lz4hc,snappy,zlib,zstd
